## Rebuttal: my mother answers what they put in (Annex E)

Rebuttal is "rebutting evidence only, unless the court, for good reasons and in the furtherance of justice, permits them to adduce evidence upon their original case" (Rule 30 §5[f]). So her testimony must answer specific defense evidence. Their own papers already open the doors:

- The deed (Def. Exh. 6) recites that Article 1623 "had been complied with," that is, that the co-owners were notified.

- The receipts (Def. Exh. 5) are headed "Heirs of Mary W. Keesey Estate."

- Erwin swears the purchase began "first with Ben Llamanzares" and that Cesar showed the SPA "as proof he was authorized to sell."

- Salvador swears no one questioned his father's authority and that his father dealt with the Agcaoili office.

- If they offer her 2023 affidavit of loss as ratification, she explains it.

A door opens only when they offer that evidence at trial, so on cross please put each point on the record anyway, and I will order every transcript. On 9 December, rest _subject to rebuttal_ and ask for rebuttal dates after 10 March 2027 and for memoranda (Rule 30 §5[g]).

**Two decisions for you.** First, the Judicial Affidavit Rule ties affidavits to the pre-trial (§2[a]); does her rebuttal affidavit need the once-only leave for late filing (§10[a])? If so, that leave is kept for her, and Mrs. King stays on Exhibit L. Second, how she testifies from California: videoconference on motion, or a deposition before a consul (Rule 23). I will have her answers gathered by 31 October.
